name: Gilt market
summary: 30-year gilt yield eased to 5.64% on 24 Nov and the 10-year to about 5.2% on 23 Nov; long yields stay elevated
state: The 30-year gilt yield fell to about 5.64% on 24 Nov, roughly 10bp lower over the month but about 32bp above a year earlier (Trading Economics). The 10-year rose above 5.35% on 16 Nov as markets priced an 80% chance of a December Bank of England rise, then fell to about 5.2% by 23 Nov (Trading Economics). The 10-year's monthly move is inside the 40bp line; Watch is kept under hysteresis because long yields remain near their recent multi-decade highs, and no weak auction or BoE intervention was found.
for_you: Gilt yields feed through to fixed mortgage rates and annuity rates over time. Higher long-term borrowing costs also raise the cost of government debt interest.
rubric_hit: Watch: 30y gilt still near multi-decade highs (5.64% on 24 Nov); 10y monthly move under 40bp; no BoE intervention

sources.title: Trading Economics — UK gilt yields surge as rate hike expectations mount

why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
